title: A review approves the diff Kriya PRESENTED (bound by review id, candidate digest and per-file diff digests). After approval the workflow runs its regression gates in the same sandbox and then applies; it does not re-digest the candidate against the approved digest before applying (independent review F4, TRACED as likely, not fully traced).
current_behaviour: TRACED: mostly mitigated, with a residual gap. (1) CANDIDATE-VERIFIED-DIGEST-BINDING-001: development_loop.py:606-613 binds the exact terminal batch (bytes sha256 + mode + base, kriya/workflow/verification_binding.py:63-83) BEFORE the approval gate (development_loop.py:898). terminal_commit.commit_terminal_candidate recomputes it from the batch it writes and refuses any difference with VERIFIED_CANDIDATE_EVIDENCE_STALE before the first workspace byte (terminal_commit.py:253-259, verification_binding.py:84-98; pinned by tests/test_authority_invariants.py:132). Any worktree edit or mode change after the binding, including between approval and commit, is refused. (2) In HITL, execution after source approval runs under a guard comparing against that binding (development_loop.py:922-940). Residual: the human approves a diff built from text-decoded worktree reads (stage_apply.py:136-153, errors='replace', no mode), bound by `candidate_digest` over diff text (kriya/policy/approval.py:247-250). No step compares the review's identity with the verified/applied binding, so reviewed==applied holds only transitively (same worktree read), not as an asserted identity. Non-UTF-8 bytes and mode are not visible in what was approved.
contract_ref: handover/MODULARIZATION/MODULE-CONTRACTS.md section 4 `CandidateIdentity  # binds reviewed == built == tested == runtime == applied`; SLICE-PLAN C1 invariant; kriya/policy/authority.py:44-47 ARRIVES_LATER typed_approval_requests -> G4 ('the CandidateIdentity equality test')
evidence: related open row DIFF-APPLIED-BYTES-BINDING-001 (P2, OPEN) - near duplicate
class_reasoning: The target architecture explicitly defines one CandidateIdentity binding reviewed == built == tested == runtime == applied, and assigns its equality check to G4. Today the review record is not tied to that identity: the binding is enforced only from verification to apply, and the review/apply link is transitive. That is an evidence-binding gap in the defined architecture, so A, not B. The row's literal claim ('no re-digest before apply') is largely overtaken by CANDIDATE-VERIFIED-DIGEST-BINDING-001, so it is not fully A-as-written. It is not C either, because the reviewed identity is still unbound and the presented diff can hide bytes and mode. Exploitability in-process is INFERRED to be very low, since a change after the binding is refused at commit. It overlaps DIFF-APPLIED-BYTES-BINDING-001: close both together.
reproducer: needs construction: in the run_direct harness (tests/test_greenfield_direct_plan_runtime.py), approve a review whose presented diff hides a non-UTF-8 byte or a mode bit; assert the review record's identity equals the applied CandidateIdentity (fails today: no such identity exists); plus a tamper-after-approval-before-commit case (expected refused today by VERIFIED_CANDIDATE_EVIDENCE_STALE)

title: A decision file and the launch record are ordinary files under <folder>/.kriya/control/launches: a local actor with the same user's filesystem write access could write a bound-looking decision file (all identities are readable from the launch record) or run `kriya launch-decision` itself. Kriya cannot hold a secret a same-user process cannot read.
current_behaviour: TRACED: decisions are files under <workspace>/.kriya/control/launches. control/launch_approval.decide (launch_approval.py:174-236) accepts a decision for any caller that presents the readable launch id, review id and candidate digest, while the waiting run's lock is held. Writes are exclusive (os.link) and the waiter re-checks bindings, expiry and the ownership stamp. The Developer's file writes cannot touch .kriya (kriya/policy/filesystem.py:116-117 TRUSTED_CONTROL_DIRECTORIES). But candidate code that Kriya itself EXECUTES (build/tests/runtime verification) runs inside <workspace>/.kriya/worktrees/candidate-* (kriya/workflow/worktree.py:45,89), and by default it is uncontained (autonomy.contained_execution_required=False, config.py:523; sandbox.py only restricts env and rlimits). INFERRED: such code, or a process it detaches, can reach ../../control/launches or run `kriya launch-decision` and answer a later pending review (the runtime-command review, or the next candidate's source review). Under OCI containment only the worktree is mounted RW (containment.py MountSpec / containment_oci.py), so .kriya/control would be out of reach (INFERRED, not run).
contract_ref: registry closure_evidence ('same-user filesystem actors are already inside the trust boundary'); 09_FINAL_APPROVAL_AND_CERTIFICATION.md:70; kriya/tools/sandbox.py:11-19 (uncontained execution does not stop disk access); cross-cutting invariant 'Model text is evidence, never authority'
class_reasoning: If the threat model treats every same-user process as trusted, this is a documented intentional boundary (E). Consume-time checks are tested in tests/test_launch_approval.py, and uncontained executed code could in any case write the owner workspace directly. In that reading the decision forgery is subsumed by the documented uncontained-execution limitation. But the row's own framing ('a model/tool with write access to .kriya/control') points at a narrower actor. That actor is model-authored code that Kriya itself runs, in a worktree that sits under the same .kriya directory as the decision files. It could convert one human approval (of source) into a forged later approval (of a command or a new candidate), which would break 'model output is never authority' (A). Which reading applies is a threat-model choice the evidence cannot settle.
owner_question: Is code that Kriya itself executes from a model-authored candidate (tests, runtime verification, possibly a detached child of them), running uncontained by default as the same user inside <workspace>/.kriya/worktrees, inside the trust boundary for HUMAN DECISIONS? If NO -> A (protect .kriya/control from executed candidate code: decision channel/key outside the workspace, or make containment default when a desktop review is pending; size MEDIUM, owner AUTHORITY + EXECUTION, slice NEW or L1). If YES -> E (document explicitly in the threat model that HITL decisions are only as strong as uncontained execution, and that contained_execution_required is the mitigation).
